items.title: 美債殖利率攀升重創小型股！羅素2000瀕臨修正 資金轉向「科技七巨頭」避波動
items.title_en: Rising U.S. Treasury Yields Cripple Small‑Cap Stocks; Russell 2000 Nears Correction as Funds Shift to the “Big Seven Tech” for Stability
paras: 美國公債殖利率飆升，正在重創股市中一些容易被忽略的部分，以小型股為主的羅素2000指數正逐步逼近修正區域，反觀投資人對科技股重燃熱情，讓標普500指數今年來表現一舉超車。
原本市場預期，今年健康的經濟成長將推動股市漲勢擴大到更多類股，然而羅素2000指數如今距離不到兩個月前創下的歷史收盤高點已經回檔9%，以周三(7日)收盤的2793.20點來計算，正瀕臨步入修正領域。
市場通常把修正定義為從近期高點下跌至少10%，這意味著羅素2000指數若收在2761.58點或更低，將正式進入修正。
小型股指數今年來績效已落後標普500指數，這與幾周前的情況大相逕庭，主要原因是投資人重新湧入一小群人工智慧(AI)概念股，幫助大型股指數周二創新高。
FactSet數據顯示，羅素2000指數今年來上漲12.5%，標普500指數同期上漲14%。
Truist Advisory Services投資長Keith Lerner說：「近期小型股下跌背後的『第一個，也是最重要的因素』」是美國長債殖利率上升。較高的利率正帶來影響，只是科技業掩蓋了這一點。」
整體而言，過去一個月以來，大多數對利率敏感的類股都承受壓力。根據FactSet數據，自9月初以來，標普500指數當中的金融類股與房地產類股都下跌逾7%，材料類股下跌5.4%，工業類股下跌4%。
Lerner說：「對我而言，關鍵在於小型股對利率更加敏感，它們的負債較多，而且相較於大型股，浮動利率債務也更多。」
事實上，通膨疑慮、油價上漲以及美國財政赤字擴大所引發的債券殖利率上升，可能為小型股帶來估值與再融資壓力。規模較小且尚未獲利的企業，通常高度依賴充裕的浮動利率債務來支應成長。當利率大幅走高時，借貸成本可能侵蝕本來就很有限的利潤率。
面對利率節節攀升，包括「科技七巨頭」在內的大型股企業卻相對抗跌，儘管它們正為支應AI建設而大量新增債務。在波動劇烈的利率環境下，投資人正重新湧入這些公司，以及其他獲利表現亮眼的企業，尋求避風港。
近期標普500指數上漲，反映資金轉向資產負債表較強、品質較高的企業，但即使是專攻科技領域的小型股也表現不佳，根據FactSet數據，景順標普小型資訊科技類股ETF(Invesco S&P SmallCap Information Technology ETF)(PSCT)自6月30日創下歷史高點以來，已下跌10.4%。
盈透證券(Interactive Brokers)首席策略師Steve Sosnick認為，儘管經濟仍保持健康，但目前的環境對小型股並不特別有利。他形容經濟「不錯」，但也擔心經濟已由AI資料中心建設主導。
他說：「第2季GDP成長2.2%，未必能讓所有船隻一起上升。因此，我們看到的是不均衡的經濟成長，隨著利率大幅回升，這對小型股而言是一個艱難的環境。」
paras_en: U.S. Treasury yields have surged, severely hurting often‑overlooked parts of the market, with the small‑cap‑heavy Russell 2000 index edging toward a correction zone, while investors’ renewed enthusiasm for tech stocks has helped the S&P 500 outpace them this year.

The market had originally expected that healthy economic growth this year would broaden the rally to more sectors, but the Russell 2000 is already down 9% from the historic closing high set less than two months ago, sitting at 2,793.20 points on Wednesday (the 7th) and teetering on the edge of a correction.
A correction is typically defined as a drop of at least 10% from a recent peak, meaning the Russell 2000 would officially enter correction territory if it closes at 2,761.58 points or lower.

Small‑cap performance has lagged the S&P 500 this year, a stark reversal from a few weeks ago, mainly because investors have poured back into a handful of AI‑related stocks, boosting large‑cap indices to a new high on Tuesday.
FactSet data show the Russell 2000 is up 12.5% year‑to‑date, while the S&P 500 has risen 14% over the same period.

Keith Lerner, chief investment officer at Truist Advisory Services, said the "first and most important factor" behind the recent small‑cap decline is the rise in long‑term U.S. Treasury yields, noting that higher rates are having an impact that the tech sector tends to mask.

Overall, over the past month most rate‑sensitive sectors have felt pressure. FactSet data indicate that since early September, financials and real estate within the S&P 500 have each fallen more than 7%, materials down 5.4% and industrials down 4%.
Lerner added, "For me, the key is that small caps are more rate‑sensitive—they carry more debt and, compared with large caps, have a higher proportion of floating‑rate liabilities."

In fact, inflation worries, rising oil prices and a widening U.S. fiscal deficit have pushed bond yields higher, creating valuation and refinancing pressure for small caps. Smaller, unprofitable firms often rely heavily on abundant floating‑rate debt to fund growth, and sharply higher rates can erode their already thin profit margins.

Facing climbing rates, large‑cap firms—including the so‑called “Big Seven Tech” companies—have been relatively resilient despite adding substantial debt to fund AI initiatives. In a volatile rate environment, investors are flowing back into these firms and other high‑quality, profitable companies as safe havens.

The recent S&P 500 rally reflects a shift toward companies with stronger balance sheets and higher quality, yet even tech‑focused small caps have struggled. FactSet shows the Invesco S&P SmallCap Information Technology ETF (PSCT) has fallen 10.4% since its June 30 peak.

Steve Sosnick, chief strategist at Interactive Brokers, believes that although the economy remains healthy, the current backdrop is not especially friendly to small caps. He describes the economy as "pretty good" but worries it is becoming dominated by AI data‑center construction.
He said, "Q2 GDP growth of 2.2% may not lift all boats. So we see uneven economic growth, and with rates climbing sharply, that creates a tough environment for small‑cap stocks."

items.title: 不到一年裁員3萬人 亞馬遜一邊瘦身 一邊豪賭AI
items.title_en: Amazon Cuts 30,000 Jobs in Less Than a Year While Betting Big on AI
paras: 多名亞馬遜(AMZN-US) 員工周二（6日）透露，公司多個業務部門當天啟動新一輪裁員，據《Business Insider》周四報導，有員工在亞馬遜一個擁有近3.7萬名成員的Slack頻道中發文，稱自己收到了崗位被撤銷的郵件通知。
該頻道隨即被大量提問淹沒，員工關心的焦點集中在遣散補償方案、內部崗位投遞權限，以及本輪裁員是否會繼續擴大等方面。
消息人士透露，本輪裁員覆蓋客服、平台支持、亞馬遜零售業務的工程崗位等多個單元，印度和英國的團隊也在波及之列。
一位熟悉情況的人士說，受影響員工總數不到1,000人。亞馬遜發言人隨後向《Business Insider》證實，公司周二裁撤了少量職位，主要集中在門市業務部門。
此次裁員是亞馬遜自2025年10月以來多輪人員調整的延續。
2025年10月28日，亞馬遜人力資源高級副總裁貝絲·加萊蒂（Beth Galetti）發布全員備忘錄，宣布裁撤約1.4萬個企業崗位，約佔企業員工總數4%，涉及AWS雲端服務、設備與服務、廣告、Prime Video、HR等多個核心部門。
當時亞馬遜全球員工約156萬人，其中企業和技術崗位約35萬人。亞馬遜表示，即使在其他領域裁員，也將繼續在戰略領域招聘。
僅僅三個月後，2026年1月28日，亞馬遜又宣布裁減1.6萬名企業級員工，波及範圍擴展至AWS的Bedrock、AI雲端服務、Redshift、數據倉庫平台以及ProServe咨詢部門，地區上覆蓋美國、英國和印度。
有員工反映，裁員通知郵件送達後，其辦公門禁權限被即時停用，需由安保人員陪同離開亞馬遜辦公室。
據第三方追蹤平台Layoffs.fyi統計，今年1月至9月，亞馬遜已裁減約1.7萬人。算上2025年10月的1.4萬人，過去不到一年時間內，亞馬遜累計裁員人數已經超過3萬人。其中超過七成集中於L5-L7職級中層管理崗位，被裁對象以白領和技術人員為主。
不過，外界注意到一個耐人尋味的反差，亞馬遜一邊大規模裁人，一邊將資本開支推向歷史新高。
亞馬遜2026年資本支出預計約2,000億美元，絕大部分投向AI基礎設施（資料中心、自研晶片和網路設備），較2025年激增近60%‌。
執行長安迪·賈西在4月致股東信中確認了這一計畫，並強調這是為了抓住千載難逢的機會，而非一時興起。‌‌這相當於裁減白領省下的成本，被大規模轉入算力投資。
paras_en: Several Amazon (AMZN-US) employees disclosed on Tuesday (June 6) that the company launched a new round of layoffs across multiple business units. According to Business Insider on Thursday, an employee posted in a Slack channel with nearly 37,000 members that they had received an email notification that their position had been eliminated.
The channel was quickly flooded with questions, with employees focusing on severance packages, internal job application access, and whether this round of layoffs would expand further.
Sources say the layoffs cover customer service, platform support, engineering roles in Amazon Retail, and also affect teams in India and the UK.

An insider said the total number of affected employees is less than 1,000. An Amazon spokesperson later confirmed to Business Insider that the Tuesday cuts involved a small number of positions, mainly in the retail operations division.
This round continues Amazon’s series of workforce adjustments since October 2025.

On October 28, 2025, Amazon HR senior vice president Beth Galetti sent a company-wide memo announcing the elimination of about 14,000 corporate positions, roughly 4% of corporate staff, affecting core units such as AWS, Devices & Services, Advertising, Prime Video, and HR.

At that time Amazon had about 1.56 million global employees, with about 350,000 in corporate and technical roles. Amazon said it would continue hiring in strategic areas even as it cut jobs elsewhere.

Three months later, on January 28, 2026, Amazon announced another cut of 16,000 corporate employees, expanding the scope to AWS Bedrock, AI cloud services, Redshift, data warehouse platforms, and ProServe consulting, covering the U.S., U.K., and India.
Some employees reported that after receiving the layoff notice, their office access was immediately revoked and they had to leave the Amazon office with security escort.

According to third‑party tracker Layoffs.fyi, Amazon has cut about 17,000 people from January to September 2026. Adding the 14,000 from October 2025, Amazon has laid off more than 30,000 people in less than a year, with over 70% of the cuts concentrated in L5‑L7 mid‑management roles, primarily white‑collar and technical staff.
However, observers note a striking contrast: Amazon is cutting jobs on a massive scale while driving capital expenditures to record highs.

Amazon’s 2026 capital spend is projected at about $200 billion, with the vast majority directed toward AI infrastructure—data centers, in‑house chips, and networking equipment—an increase of nearly 60% from 2025.

In a shareholder letter in April, CEO Andy Jassy confirmed this plan and emphasized that it is about seizing a once‑in‑a‑lifetime opportunity, not a fleeting impulse. This effectively reallocates the savings from white‑collar cuts into large‑scale compute investment.

items.title: 華爾街對Marvell超樂觀 亮眼財測點燃成長潛力
items.title_en: Wall Street Overly Optimistic on Marvell; Bright Financial Forecast Ignites Growth Potential
paras: 《巴隆周刊》周三(7日)報導，邁威爾科技(Marvell Technology)(MRVL-US)獲得華爾街大量讚賞，但對於一家預期未來5年營收每年將成長55%至60%的公司而言，這樣的看好或許並不令人意外。
根據FactSet數據，截至本周已有至少18名分析師上調Marvell的目標價。這是在這家晶片與網路設備公司於紐約舉行的投資人日公布積極成長目標後出現的反應。
StoneX分析師Cody Acree便是其中一位看多者，他周二晚間將Marvell目標價從275美元上調至375美元。Acree在研究報告中寫道，這次投資人日「重新定義了Marvell AI商機的規模與持續時間」。
Acree給予Marvell股票「買進」評級。他的新目標價意味著，與周二收盤價相比，仍有31%的上漲空間。
Oppenheimer分析師Rick Schafer周三也表示，「市場氣氛明確的偏樂觀，表現超出預期，因為管理層大幅上調了財務目標。」他並將Marvell目標價從325美元上調至425美元，同時給予Marvell股票「優於大盤」評級。
推動華爾街分析師紛紛上調目標價的主要催化劑，是Marvell亮眼的財測。該公司預估，2031會計年度調整後每股盈餘(EPS)將超過30美元，營收則達到700億至900億美元。作為對照，2026會計年度Marvell每股盈餘為2.84美元，營收為82億美元。
Marvell股價周三下跌1.5%，收在282.73美元，此前周二才大漲5.8%。周二股價在執行長Matt Murphy公布營收目標後立即走高。
今年以來，Marvell股價已上漲238%。隨著AI熱潮推升晶片與網路產品需求，Marvell股價持續受到市場追捧。
paras_en: Baron Weekly reported on Wednesday (the 7th) that Marvell Technology (MRVL-US) has received abundant praise from Wall Street, but for a company that expects revenue to grow 55% to 60% annually over the next five years, such optimism may not be surprising.

According to FactSet data, at least 18 analysts have raised Marvell’s price target as of this week. This reaction came after the chip and networking equipment company announced aggressive growth goals at its investor day in New York.

StoneX analyst Cody Acree is one of the bullish voices; on Tuesday night he lifted Marvell’s price target from $275 to $375. In his research note, Acree wrote that the investor day "redefined the scale and duration of Marvell’s AI opportunity."
Acree gave Marvell a "Buy" rating. His new target implies a 31% upside from Tuesday’s closing price.

Oppenheimer analyst Rick Schafer also said on Wednesday that "the market sentiment is clearly optimistic, outperforming expectations, because management significantly raised its financial targets." He raised Marvell’s target from $325 to $425 and assigned an "Outperform" rating.

The main catalyst driving analysts to raise targets is Marvell’s impressive financial outlook. The company forecasts adjusted FY 2031 earnings per share (EPS) of over $30 and revenue of $70 billion to $90 billion. By comparison, FY 2026 EPS is $2.84 and revenue $8.2 billion.
Marvell’s stock fell 1.5% on Wednesday, closing at $282.73, after having jumped 5.8% on Tuesday. The Tuesday rally came immediately after CEO Matt Murphy announced the revenue targets.
Since the start of the year, Marvell’s share price has risen 238%. Fueled by the AI boom driving demand for chips and networking products, the stock continues to attract strong market interest.

items.title: 市值近25兆美元富可敵國！科技七巨頭包辦三成資本支出  「插頭一拔」全球震盪
items.title_en: Nearly $25 trillion in Market Value, Wealth Rivaling Nations! The Seven Tech Giants Account for About 30% of Capital Spending – Pull One Plug and the World Shakes
paras: 「科技七巨頭」(Magnificent Seven)合計市值接近25兆美元，如果這群科技公司是一個國家，其經濟規模將位居全球第二，超越中國、德國、日本與英國且正逼近美國。當它們成為一股足以撼動經濟的力量，讓人不免擔心經濟力量異常集中所可能產生的問題。
這七家大型科技股包括Alphabet(GOOGL-US)、亞馬遜(AMZN-US)、蘋果(APPL-US)、Meta Platforms(META-US)、微軟(MSFT-US)、輝達(NVDA-US)與特斯拉(TSLA-US)。
Apex Fintech Solutions首席市場分析師暨風險副總裁Mike Treacy說：「這些公司生產的所有產品與提供的服務，就是全世界運轉所依賴的東西，而當你拔掉其中任何一個插頭，一切就會崩潰。」
在這樣的規模下，「科技七巨頭」賺多少錢、花多少錢、借多少錢，以及雇用哪些人，其影響都遠遠超出華爾街。
Treacy指出，這些公司的總體經濟影響「非常巨大」，因為它們往往「成群結隊」行動。例如，2022年利率上升終結廉價資金時代，迫使許多企業、尤其是科技公司，從「不惜一切代價追求成長」的思維，轉向重視獲利能力與削減成本。
近來，人工智慧(AI)熱潮則推動其中許多公司大幅提高資本支出。根據Apex Fintech Solutions與彭博彙整的數據，2026年到目前為止，「科技七巨頭」加上SpaceX(SPCX-US)每年的資本支出約為5800億美元，而標普500指數其餘企業一年的資本支出合計約為1.4兆美元。
換句話說，「科技七巨頭」與SpaceX約占標普500指數總資本支出的30%，凸顯企業投資如今已高度集中在少數大型公司。
令人擔心的是，如果其中一家大型公司開始削減AI建設的支出，其他公司可能跟進，進而導致科技投資全面縮減，並對市場造成重大干擾。
Treacy說：「世界由美國企業運轉，這很好。我們為全世界提供動力，這很好。但如果資本支出的潮流發生轉變，那麼不只美國，全球經濟成長都將面臨一些挑戰。」
paras_en: The “Magnificent Seven” tech giants have a combined market value close to $25 trillion. If these companies were a country, its economy would rank second worldwide, surpassing China, Germany, Japan and the United Kingdom and closing in on the United States. Their sheer economic heft raises concerns about the risks of such concentrated power.
The seven large‑cap tech stocks are Alphabet (GOOGL‑US), Amazon (AMZN‑US), Apple (AAPL‑US), Meta Platforms (META‑US), Microsoft (MSFT‑US), Nvidia (NVDA‑US) and Tesla (TSLA‑US).

Mike Treacy, chief market analyst and vice‑president of risk at Apex Fintech Solutions, said: “All the products these companies make and the services they provide are what the world runs on, and if you pull any one of those plugs, everything collapses.”
At this scale, how much the “Magnificent Seven” earn, spend, borrow and whom they employ has impacts that far exceed Wall Street’s own sphere.

Treacy noted that the overall economic impact of these firms is “enormous” because they tend to act “in packs.” For example, when interest rates rose in 2022 and ended the era of cheap capital, many firms—especially tech companies—shifted from a “grow at all costs” mindset to one that emphasizes profitability and cost cutting.

Recently, the AI boom has driven many of these companies to sharply increase capital expenditures. According to data compiled by Apex Fintech Solutions and Bloomberg, through 2026 the “Magnificent Seven” together with SpaceX (SPCX‑US) have spent roughly $580 billion per year on capex, while the rest of the S&P 500 companies collectively spend about $1.4 trillion annually.

In other words, the “Magnificent Seven” plus SpaceX account for roughly 30 % of total S&P 500 capital spending, highlighting how corporate investment is now heavily concentrated in a handful of mega‑firms.

The worrying scenario is that if one of these large firms begins to cut back AI‑related spending, others may follow, leading to a broad reduction in tech investment and causing significant market disruption.

Treacy said: “The world runs on American companies, and that’s a good thing. We power the globe, and that’s a good thing. But if the tide of capital spending turns, it won’t just be the United States—global economic growth will face challenges.”

items.title: Anthropic僅值1500億美元？遭評「2026年最荒謬IPO」
items.title_en: Anthropic Valued at Only $150 B? Called the "Most Ridiculous IPO of 2026"
paras: 《CNBC》報導，隨著Anthropic朝著在那斯達克掛牌、潛在市值達2兆美元的方向邁進，一家研究機構卻僅給予這家AI公司1,500億美元估值，並警告華爾街即將面臨「投資人輕信程度前所未有的考驗」。
獨立金融研究機構New Constructs周二發布報告，將Anthropic即將進行的首次公開募股稱為「2026年最荒謬IPO」。
New Constructs估計，若要達到Anthropic所期望的估值，該公司必須創造出全球市值最高的科技公司輝達(NVDA-US)過去一年獲利的兩倍。輝達過去四季淨利潤已超過1,900億美元。
而據《路透社》引用Anthropic招股說明書外洩版本的報導，Anthropic 2025年營收為46億美元，但淨損高達420億美元。
Anthropic不斷攀升的營運虧損，加上大量開源模型帶來的競爭，讓New Constructs得出結論：「我們認為Anthropic並沒有一個可行的商業模式。」
該機構寫道，「自從開源模型出現以來，很明顯的，封閉式模型將難以創造獲利。」
New Constructs創辦人兼執行長David Trainer在華爾街以看空IPO聞名，而且過去也曾成功預測部分IPO問題。
New Constructs曾在2019年WeWork計劃上市前，稱其為「2019年最荒謬的IPO」。當時WeWork私人市場估值曾達470億美元，但New Constructs發布報告僅6周後，WeWork便因需求疲弱，以及市場對其財務狀況的強烈批評而撤回IPO計畫。WeWork最終於2023年申請破產。
New Constructs寫道，「雖然Anthropic對社會的貢獻遠高於WeWork，但若估值達到2兆美元，其IPO帶來的風險將放大更多，也可能成為對美國資本市場更大的掠奪。」該機構補充稱，這場IPO的目的並不是為公開市場投資人創造財富，而是為公司的華爾街支持者提供流動性。
New Constructs在2021年Allbirds(BIRD-US)上市時同樣看空。這家鞋類公司當年在那斯達克掛牌，首日交易估值一度達到41億美元。今年稍早，Allbirds將旗下資產出售給American Exchange Group，交易估值約為3,900萬美元，並在此過程中轉向AI領域。
不過，Trainer的公司也曾有看走眼的案例。New Constructs評選的「2020年最荒謬IPO」是DoorDash(DASH-US)，該機構當時也將DoorDash與WeWork相提並論，稱這家外送公司「同樣處於不利地位」。
然而，DoorDash在公開市場的表現相當穩健。該公司2020年12月上市首日股價大漲，市值突破600億美元，此後更進一步攀升至830億美元。
Trainer在2021年受訪時也承認，「瘋狂的事情確實會發生」，而New Constructs並非總能做出正確判斷。「我不能讓這件事困擾我。我必須忠於自己認為正確的判斷。」
Anthropic至今仍未公開招股說明書，因此New Constructs並未看過正式申報文件。不過，該機構引用了多項已經曝光數據，包括《紐約時報》的報導。該報去年9月稱，Anthropic預計到2026年底，年化營收將達到1,000億美元。
Anthropic則在7月底表示，截至當時公司的年化營收已較去年同期成長7倍，達到650億美元。
New Constructs報告還指出，Anthropic曾警告AI可能對人類構成「災難性或存亡級風險」，這也是投資人應該避開這場IPO的另一項理由。
New Constructs寫道，「雖然我們並沒有幸運的成為Anthropic選擇性披露S-1文件的少數對象之一，但外洩財務數據的相關報導，已經揭露了足以讓我們評估這場IPO龐大投資風險的資訊。」
paras_en: CNBC reported that as Anthropic moves toward a Nasdaq listing with a potential market value of $2 trillion, a research firm has assigned the AI company a valuation of just $150 billion and warned that Wall Street is about to face an unprecedented test of investors' gullibility.
Independent financial research firm New Constructs released a report on Tuesday calling Anthropic's upcoming initial public offering the "Most Ridiculous IPO of 2026."

New Constructs estimates that to achieve the valuation Anthropic seeks, the company would have to generate twice the profit that Nvidia (NVDA-US), the world’s most valuable tech firm, earned over the past year. Nvidia’s net profit over the last four quarters has already exceeded $190 billion.
According to a Reuters story citing a leaked version of Anthropic’s prospectus, the company’s 2025 revenue is projected at $4.6 billion, but its net loss would be a staggering $42 billion.
Anthropic’s ever‑growing operating losses, combined with intense competition from open‑source models, lead New Constructs to conclude: "We believe Anthropic does not have a viable business model."
The firm wrote, "Since the advent of open‑source models, it has become clear that closed‑source models will struggle to generate profit."
New Constructs founder and CEO David Trainer is known on Wall Street for his bearish stance on IPOs and has previously correctly predicted problems with several offerings.

In 2019, New Constructs labeled WeWork’s planned listing as "the most ridiculous IPO of 2019." At the time, WeWork’s private‑market valuation had reached $47 billion, but just six weeks after the firm’s report, WeWork withdrew its IPO amid weak demand and harsh criticism of its finances, eventually filing for bankruptcy in 2023.

New Constructs wrote, "Although Anthropic’s contribution to society far exceeds that of WeWork, a $2 trillion valuation would magnify the risks of its IPO and could become a greater predatory force on U.S. capital markets." The firm added that the purpose of the offering is not to create wealth for public investors but to provide liquidity for Anthropic’s Wall Street backers.

New Constructs also took a bearish view when Allbirds (BIRD-US) went public in 2021. The footwear company debuted on Nasdaq with a peak first‑day valuation of $4.1 billion. Earlier this year, Allbirds sold its assets to the American Exchange Group for roughly $39 million and pivoted toward AI.
However, Trainer’s firm has had missteps. Its "most ridiculous IPO of 2020" pick was DoorDash (DASH-US), which it then compared to WeWork, calling the delivery firm "similarly disadvantaged."
DoorDash’s market performance has been solid. The company’s shares surged on its December 2020 debut, pushing its market cap past $60 billion, and later climbing to about $83 billion.

In a 2021 interview, Trainer admitted, "Crazy things do happen," and that New Constructs does not always get it right. "I can’t let this bother me. I have to stay true to the judgments I believe are correct."

Anthropic has not yet released a formal prospectus, so New Constructs has not seen an official filing. The firm does cite several publicly disclosed data points, including a New York Times report that last September projected Anthropic’s annual revenue would reach $100 billion by the end of 2026.
Anthropic said at the end of July that its annualized revenue had grown seven‑fold year‑over‑year to $65 billion.

The New Constructs report also notes that Anthropic warned AI could pose "catastrophic or existential risks" to humanity, which the firm cites as another reason investors should steer clear of the IPO.

New Constructs wrote, "While we were not among the lucky few selected by Anthropic for a selective S‑1 disclosure, the leaked financial data reports have revealed enough information for us to assess the massive investment risk of this IPO."

items.title: 黃仁勳焦慮AI需求降溫！傳輝達再砸10億美元加碼人形機器人企業Figure
items.title_en: Jensen Huang Worried About Cooling AI Demand! Nvidia Adds Another $1 Billion to Humanoid Robot Company Figure
paras: 外媒最新報導指出，AI晶片巨擘輝達近期正討論向人形機器人製造商Figure追加投資10億美元，該融資計畫此前從未對外披露。輝達已是Figure的投資方，一年前曾以相同估值參與其超過10億美元的融資。Figure此輪融資的投前估值約為380億美元
《The Information》引述知情人士報導，除加碼機器人賽道外，輝達的投資版圖正持續擴大。知情人士透露，輝達也可能向兩類新創公司注資：一類是協助開發其Nemotron開源模型的公司，另一類是開發其他AI應用的團隊，例如輝達已同意斥資60億美元獲取Poolside的軟體授權並聘用其員工，以推動Nemotron模型的研發，Poolside團隊今年剛推出開放權重的Laguna AI模型。
輝達執行長黃仁勳正主導此投資佈局。儘管手握990億美元現金及證券，且現金流充沛，黃仁勳仍對公司的全球市場地位保持警惕。
他坦言，擔憂AI需求降溫或出現替代性晶片產品，因此希望透過財力推動數千個AI模型發展，降低對OpenAI等少數大客戶的依賴。在今年7月為止的半年裡，三大客戶貢獻了輝達總銷售額的44%。
一名投資AI基礎設施和應用的投資人表示，如果參與黃仁勳的戰略決策，他會盡一切努力推動數千個模型服務數千種不同場景。
paras_en: Foreign media reports that Nvidia, the AI chip giant, is currently discussing a $1 billion additional investment in humanoid robot maker Figure, a financing plan that has not been disclosed before. Nvidia is already an investor in Figure, having participated in a financing round of over $1 billion a year ago at the same valuation. Figure’s pre‑money valuation for this round is about $38 billion.

The Information, citing sources, reported that beyond expanding its robot bets, Nvidia’s investment scope is continuing to broaden. Insiders say Nvidia may also fund two types of startups: one that helps develop its open‑source Nemotron model, and another that builds other AI applications. For example, Nvidia has agreed to spend $6 billion to acquire software licenses from Poolside and hire its staff to advance Nemotron development; Poolside’s team just released the open‑weight Laguna AI model this year.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is steering this investment strategy. Even though the company holds $99 billion in cash and securities and enjoys strong cash flow, Huang remains vigilant about Nvidia’s global market position.

He admitted he worries about a slowdown in AI demand or the emergence of alternative chip products, so he wants to use Nvidia’s financial muscle to push the development of thousands of AI models and reduce reliance on a few large customers such as OpenAI. In the first half of the year through July, the three biggest customers accounted for 44 % of Nvidia’s total sales.

An investor focused on AI infrastructure and applications said that if he were part of Jensen Huang’s strategic decision‑making, he would do everything possible to drive thousands of models serving thousands of different scenarios.

items.title: 花旗調升台積電目標價至4000元 看好2027年營收成長逾四成
items.title_en: Citi Raises TSMC Target Price to NT$4,000, Bullish on Over 40% Revenue Growth by 2027
paras: 花旗看好台積電(2330-TW) 營收成長前景，預估到2027年的營收成長率可能超過40%，維持「買進」評等，並將目標價由新台幣3,800元上調至4,000元。
花旗在最新研究報告中指出，受惠於AI運算需求強勁、AI代理可能帶來額外成長空間，以及共同封裝光學（CPO）網路週期興起，台積電到2027年的營收成長率可能超過40%。
花旗分析師表示，台積電多數AI晶片客戶，包括輝達(NVDA-US) 、AMD(AMD-US)及博通(AVGO-US) ，預計成長將加速，帶動台積電明年AI相關營收可能接近倍增。
除了既有AI運算需求，AI代理帶來的潛在成長空間，以及CPO網路週期的興起，也是花旗看好台積電營收展望的因素。
隨著AI晶片客戶成長加快，花旗預期，市場對台積電獲利的平均預估將持續上修。此次調高目標價，也反映花旗對其強勁營收前景的看法。
資本支出方面，花旗預估，在營收前景支撐下，台積電2027年與2028年的資本支出可能進一步提高，分別達810億美元及900億美元。
花旗在看好AI相關營收成長的同時，也預期台積電未來兩年的資本支出規模將持續擴大。
高盛日前也將台積電目標價由3,100元上調至3,300元，維持「買進」評級，並調高資本支出預估，主因是看好AI需求持續擴張。
高盛分析師Evelyn Yu指出，AI需求持續擴及GPU、網路晶片與伺服器CPU，其中代理型AI帶動CPU需求增強，是過去一年來的關鍵變化。
該行預估，以美元計算，台積電2026年及2027年營收將分別年增42%與36.9%，毛利率則達67.2%與67.5%。
隨著AI需求擴張，高盛也將台積電2027年及2028年資本支出預估，由780億及820億美元，均上調至850億美元。
paras_en: Citi is optimistic about TSMC (2330-TW) revenue growth prospects, estimating that revenue growth could exceed 40% by 2027, maintaining a "Buy" rating and raising the target price from NT$3,800 to NT$4,000.

In its latest research report, Citi notes that strong AI computing demand, additional growth potential from AI agents, and the emergence of the Co‑Packaged Optics (CPO) network cycle could push TSMC's revenue growth rate past 40% by 2027.

Citi analysts say that most of TSMC's AI chip customers, including Nvidia (NVDA-US), AMD (AMD-US) and Broadcom (AVGO-US), are expected to accelerate growth, potentially nearly doubling TSMC's AI‑related revenue next year.
Beyond existing AI computing demand, the potential growth from AI agents and the rise of the CPO network cycle are also factors behind Citi's positive revenue outlook for TSMC.
As AI chip customers grow faster, Citi expects market estimates of TSMC's earnings to be continually revised upward. The target‑price increase reflects Citi's view of a strong revenue outlook.
On the capital‑expenditure side, Citi projects that, supported by the revenue outlook, TSMC's capex could rise further in 2027 and 2028 to $81 billion and $90 billion respectively.
While bullish on AI‑related revenue growth, Citi also expects TSMC's capital‑expenditure scale to keep expanding over the next two years.
Goldman Sachs recently raised its TSMC target price from $3,100 to $3,300, kept a "Buy" rating, and increased its capex estimate, citing confidence in sustained AI demand expansion.
Goldman analyst Evelyn Yu highlighted that AI demand continues to spread across GPUs, networking chips and server CPUs, with agent‑type AI boosting CPU demand—a key shift over the past year.
The firm estimates that, in USD terms, TSMC's revenue will grow 42% in 2026 and 36.9% in 2027, with gross margins reaching 67.2% and 67.5% respectively.
With AI demand expanding, Goldman also raised its capex forecasts for TSMC in 2027 and 2028 from $78 billion and $82 billion to $85 billion each.

items.title: 美光股價能翻3倍？分析師喊出3000美元目標價 擁AI記憶體需求和庫藏股利多
items.title_en: Micron Stock Could Triple? Analyst Sets $3,000 Target, Citing AI Memory Demand and Share‑Buyback Boost
paras: 一名分析師主張，投資人並未充分理解美光科技(MU-US)的成長潛力及其股票應有的估值，預測美光應可漲到目前水準的三倍高。
D.A. Davidson分析師Gil Luria認為，投資人尚未充分反映美光未來三到五年的預期成長軌跡。他表示，美光目前極低的估值倍數，同樣未能反映該公司的真正價值。
根據道瓊市場數據，目前美光股價僅相當於該會計年度預估獲利的約六倍。
Luria周三(7日)將美光目標價從2100美元上修至3000美元。以美光周三收盤價每股1088美元計算，新的目標價意味著股價幾乎有望增至目前水準的三倍。
Luria假設，投資人未來可能願意給予美光每1美元獲利更高的估值，而美光在明年8月結束的2027會計年度當中，EPS可享有約19倍本益比。

記憶體供不應求 美光成長潛力受看好

美光股價今年以來已上漲266%，但由於市場對獲利成長的預期超越股價漲幅，導致美光的本益比實際上已較2025年底下降。
Luria看好美光的一大理由，是記憶體晶片需求預料未來數年都將超過供給。他寫道：「記憶體是提升AI效能的槓桿。AI模型擁有更多記憶體，就能產生更好的結果。擁有更多記憶體，也能運行得更快。」
12月啟動大型庫藏股計畫 有望推升EPS
另一項值得注意的催化劑，是美光預定在12月啟動大型庫藏股計畫。屆時，美光將不再受到美國《晶片法案》(CHIPS Act)政府補助附帶的股票回購限制。
企業買回自家股票時，會讓流通在外股數減少，進而有助於提高EPS。這項效應可能成為推動美光股價上漲的重要助力。
美光周三開低走高，終場上漲4.1%至每股1088美元。
paras_en: An analyst argues that investors have not fully grasped Micron Technology’s (MU‑US) growth potential and the valuation its stock deserves, forecasting that Micron could rise to three times its current level.

D.A. Davidson analyst Gil Luria says investors have not yet priced in Micron’s expected growth trajectory over the next three to five years. He notes that Micron’s currently ultra‑low valuation multiples also fail to reflect the company’s true worth.
According to Dow Jones market data, Micron’s share price is currently only about six times its estimated earnings for the fiscal year.
On Wednesday (the 7th), Luria raised Micron’s price target from $2,100 to $3,000. With Micron closing at $1,088 on Wednesday, the new target implies a near‑tripling of the current price.

Luria assumes investors may be willing to assign a higher multiple to each dollar of Micron’s earnings, and that Micron could enjoy roughly a 19‑times price‑to‑earnings ratio in the fiscal year ending August 2027.

Memory shortage fuels optimism about Micron’s growth potential. Micron’s stock has risen 266% so far this year, but because profit‑growth expectations outpace the price rise, Micron’s P/E ratio has actually fallen since the end of 2025.

Luria’s bullish view is largely driven by the expectation that demand for memory chips will exceed supply for several years. He writes: “Memory is a lever for boosting AI performance. The more memory an AI model has, the better the results it can produce. More memory also enables faster operation.”
Micron plans to launch a large‑scale share‑buyback program in December, which could lift EPS.

Another notable catalyst is Micron’s scheduled launch of a major share‑repurchase program in December. At that point, Micron will no longer be subject to the stock‑buyback restrictions tied to U.S. CHIPS Act government subsidies.
When a company buys back its own shares, the number of shares outstanding declines, which can help raise EPS. This effect could become a key driver of Micron’s stock appreciation.
Micron opened lower on Wednesday but rallied to close up 4.1% at $1,088 per share.

items.title: 美債殖利率攀升重創小型股！羅素2000瀕臨修正 資金轉向「科技七巨頭」避波動
items.title_en: Rising U.S. Treasury Yields Cripple Small‑Cap Stocks; Russell 2000 Nears Correction as Funds Shift to the “Big Seven Tech” for Stability
paras: 美國公債殖利率飆升，正在重創股市中一些容易被忽略的部分，以小型股為主的羅素2000指數正逐步逼近修正區域，反觀投資人對科技股重燃熱情，讓標普500指數今年來表現一舉超車。
原本市場預期，今年健康的經濟成長將推動股市漲勢擴大到更多類股，然而羅素2000指數如今距離不到兩個月前創下的歷史收盤高點已經回檔9%，以周三(7日)收盤的2793.20點來計算，正瀕臨步入修正領域。
市場通常把修正定義為從近期高點下跌至少10%，這意味著羅素2000指數若收在2761.58點或更低，將正式進入修正。
小型股指數今年來績效已落後標普500指數，這與幾周前的情況大相逕庭，主要原因是投資人重新湧入一小群人工智慧(AI)概念股，幫助大型股指數周二創新高。
FactSet數據顯示，羅素2000指數今年來上漲12.5%，標普500指數同期上漲14%。
Truist Advisory Services投資長Keith Lerner說：「近期小型股下跌背後的『第一個，也是最重要的因素』」是美國長債殖利率上升。較高的利率正帶來影響，只是科技業掩蓋了這一點。」
整體而言，過去一個月以來，大多數對利率敏感的類股都承受壓力。根據FactSet數據，自9月初以來，標普500指數當中的金融類股與房地產類股都下跌逾7%，材料類股下跌5.4%，工業類股下跌4%。
Lerner說：「對我而言，關鍵在於小型股對利率更加敏感，它們的負債較多，而且相較於大型股，浮動利率債務也更多。」
事實上，通膨疑慮、油價上漲以及美國財政赤字擴大所引發的債券殖利率上升，可能為小型股帶來估值與再融資壓力。規模較小且尚未獲利的企業，通常高度依賴充裕的浮動利率債務來支應成長。當利率大幅走高時，借貸成本可能侵蝕本來就很有限的利潤率。
面對利率節節攀升，包括「科技七巨頭」在內的大型股企業卻相對抗跌，儘管它們正為支應AI建設而大量新增債務。在波動劇烈的利率環境下，投資人正重新湧入這些公司，以及其他獲利表現亮眼的企業，尋求避風港。
近期標普500指數上漲，反映資金轉向資產負債表較強、品質較高的企業，但即使是專攻科技領域的小型股也表現不佳，根據FactSet數據，景順標普小型資訊科技類股ETF(Invesco S&P SmallCap Information Technology ETF)(PSCT)自6月30日創下歷史高點以來，已下跌10.4%。
盈透證券(Interactive Brokers)首席策略師Steve Sosnick認為，儘管經濟仍保持健康，但目前的環境對小型股並不特別有利。他形容經濟「不錯」，但也擔心經濟已由AI資料中心建設主導。
他說：「第2季GDP成長2.2%，未必能讓所有船隻一起上升。因此，我們看到的是不均衡的經濟成長，隨著利率大幅回升，這對小型股而言是一個艱難的環境。」
paras_en: U.S. Treasury yields have surged, severely hurting often‑overlooked parts of the market, with the small‑cap‑heavy Russell 2000 index edging toward a correction zone, while investors’ renewed enthusiasm for tech stocks has helped the S&P 500 outpace them this year.

The market had originally expected that healthy economic growth this year would broaden the rally to more sectors, but the Russell 2000 is already down 9% from the historic closing high set less than two months ago, sitting at 2,793.20 points on Wednesday (the 7th) and teetering on the edge of a correction.
A correction is typically defined as a drop of at least 10% from a recent peak, meaning the Russell 2000 would officially enter correction territory if it closes at 2,761.58 points or lower.

Small‑cap performance has lagged the S&P 500 this year, a stark reversal from a few weeks ago, mainly because investors have poured back into a handful of AI‑related stocks, boosting large‑cap indices to a new high on Tuesday.
FactSet data show the Russell 2000 is up 12.5% year‑to‑date, while the S&P 500 has risen 14% over the same period.

Keith Lerner, chief investment officer at Truist Advisory Services, said the "first and most important factor" behind the recent small‑cap decline is the rise in long‑term U.S. Treasury yields, noting that higher rates are having an impact that the tech sector tends to mask.

Overall, over the past month most rate‑sensitive sectors have felt pressure. FactSet data indicate that since early September, financials and real estate within the S&P 500 have each fallen more than 7%, materials down 5.4% and industrials down 4%.
Lerner added, "For me, the key is that small caps are more rate‑sensitive—they carry more debt and, compared with large caps, have a higher proportion of floating‑rate liabilities."

In fact, inflation worries, rising oil prices and a widening U.S. fiscal deficit have pushed bond yields higher, creating valuation and refinancing pressure for small caps. Smaller, unprofitable firms often rely heavily on abundant floating‑rate debt to fund growth, and sharply higher rates can erode their already thin profit margins.

Facing climbing rates, large‑cap firms—including the so‑called “Big Seven Tech” companies—have been relatively resilient despite adding substantial debt to fund AI initiatives. In a volatile rate environment, investors are flowing back into these firms and other high‑quality, profitable companies as safe havens.

The recent S&P 500 rally reflects a shift toward companies with stronger balance sheets and higher quality, yet even tech‑focused small caps have struggled. FactSet shows the Invesco S&P SmallCap Information Technology ETF (PSCT) has fallen 10.4% since its June 30 peak.

Steve Sosnick, chief strategist at Interactive Brokers, believes that although the economy remains healthy, the current backdrop is not especially friendly to small caps. He describes the economy as "pretty good" but worries it is becoming dominated by AI data‑center construction.
He said, "Q2 GDP growth of 2.2% may not lift all boats. So we see uneven economic growth, and with rates climbing sharply, that creates a tough environment for small‑cap stocks."

items.title: 不到一年裁員3萬人 亞馬遜一邊瘦身 一邊豪賭AI
items.title_en: Amazon Cuts 30,000 Jobs in Less Than a Year While Betting Big on AI
paras: 多名亞馬遜(AMZN-US) 員工周二（6日）透露，公司多個業務部門當天啟動新一輪裁員，據《Business Insider》周四報導，有員工在亞馬遜一個擁有近3.7萬名成員的Slack頻道中發文，稱自己收到了崗位被撤銷的郵件通知。
該頻道隨即被大量提問淹沒，員工關心的焦點集中在遣散補償方案、內部崗位投遞權限，以及本輪裁員是否會繼續擴大等方面。
消息人士透露，本輪裁員覆蓋客服、平台支持、亞馬遜零售業務的工程崗位等多個單元，印度和英國的團隊也在波及之列。
一位熟悉情況的人士說，受影響員工總數不到1,000人。亞馬遜發言人隨後向《Business Insider》證實，公司周二裁撤了少量職位，主要集中在門市業務部門。
此次裁員是亞馬遜自2025年10月以來多輪人員調整的延續。
2025年10月28日，亞馬遜人力資源高級副總裁貝絲·加萊蒂（Beth Galetti）發布全員備忘錄，宣布裁撤約1.4萬個企業崗位，約佔企業員工總數4%，涉及AWS雲端服務、設備與服務、廣告、Prime Video、HR等多個核心部門。
當時亞馬遜全球員工約156萬人，其中企業和技術崗位約35萬人。亞馬遜表示，即使在其他領域裁員，也將繼續在戰略領域招聘。
僅僅三個月後，2026年1月28日，亞馬遜又宣布裁減1.6萬名企業級員工，波及範圍擴展至AWS的Bedrock、AI雲端服務、Redshift、數據倉庫平台以及ProServe咨詢部門，地區上覆蓋美國、英國和印度。
有員工反映，裁員通知郵件送達後，其辦公門禁權限被即時停用，需由安保人員陪同離開亞馬遜辦公室。
據第三方追蹤平台Layoffs.fyi統計，今年1月至9月，亞馬遜已裁減約1.7萬人。算上2025年10月的1.4萬人，過去不到一年時間內，亞馬遜累計裁員人數已經超過3萬人。其中超過七成集中於L5-L7職級中層管理崗位，被裁對象以白領和技術人員為主。
不過，外界注意到一個耐人尋味的反差，亞馬遜一邊大規模裁人，一邊將資本開支推向歷史新高。
亞馬遜2026年資本支出預計約2,000億美元，絕大部分投向AI基礎設施（資料中心、自研晶片和網路設備），較2025年激增近60%‌。
執行長安迪·賈西在4月致股東信中確認了這一計畫，並強調這是為了抓住千載難逢的機會，而非一時興起。‌‌這相當於裁減白領省下的成本，被大規模轉入算力投資。
paras_en: Several Amazon (AMZN-US) employees disclosed on Tuesday (June 6) that the company launched a new round of layoffs across multiple business units. According to Business Insider on Thursday, an employee posted in a Slack channel with nearly 37,000 members that they had received an email notification that their position had been eliminated.
The channel was quickly flooded with questions, with employees focusing on severance packages, internal job application access, and whether this round of layoffs would expand further.
Sources say the layoffs cover customer service, platform support, engineering roles in Amazon Retail, and also affect teams in India and the UK.

An insider said the total number of affected employees is less than 1,000. An Amazon spokesperson later confirmed to Business Insider that the Tuesday cuts involved a small number of positions, mainly in the retail operations division.
This round continues Amazon’s series of workforce adjustments since October 2025.

On October 28, 2025, Amazon HR senior vice president Beth Galetti sent a company-wide memo announcing the elimination of about 14,000 corporate positions, roughly 4% of corporate staff, affecting core units such as AWS, Devices & Services, Advertising, Prime Video, and HR.

At that time Amazon had about 1.56 million global employees, with about 350,000 in corporate and technical roles. Amazon said it would continue hiring in strategic areas even as it cut jobs elsewhere.

Three months later, on January 28, 2026, Amazon announced another cut of 16,000 corporate employees, expanding the scope to AWS Bedrock, AI cloud services, Redshift, data warehouse platforms, and ProServe consulting, covering the U.S., U.K., and India.
Some employees reported that after receiving the layoff notice, their office access was immediately revoked and they had to leave the Amazon office with security escort.

According to third‑party tracker Layoffs.fyi, Amazon has cut about 17,000 people from January to September 2026. Adding the 14,000 from October 2025, Amazon has laid off more than 30,000 people in less than a year, with over 70% of the cuts concentrated in L5‑L7 mid‑management roles, primarily white‑collar and technical staff.
However, observers note a striking contrast: Amazon is cutting jobs on a massive scale while driving capital expenditures to record highs.

Amazon’s 2026 capital spend is projected at about $200 billion, with the vast majority directed toward AI infrastructure—data centers, in‑house chips, and networking equipment—an increase of nearly 60% from 2025.

In a shareholder letter in April, CEO Andy Jassy confirmed this plan and emphasized that it is about seizing a once‑in‑a‑lifetime opportunity, not a fleeting impulse. This effectively reallocates the savings from white‑collar cuts into large‑scale compute investment.

items.title: 華爾街對Marvell超樂觀 亮眼財測點燃成長潛力
items.title_en: Wall Street Overly Optimistic on Marvell; Bright Financial Forecast Ignites Growth Potential
paras: 《巴隆周刊》周三(7日)報導，邁威爾科技(Marvell Technology)(MRVL-US)獲得華爾街大量讚賞，但對於一家預期未來5年營收每年將成長55%至60%的公司而言，這樣的看好或許並不令人意外。
根據FactSet數據，截至本周已有至少18名分析師上調Marvell的目標價。這是在這家晶片與網路設備公司於紐約舉行的投資人日公布積極成長目標後出現的反應。
StoneX分析師Cody Acree便是其中一位看多者，他周二晚間將Marvell目標價從275美元上調至375美元。Acree在研究報告中寫道，這次投資人日「重新定義了Marvell AI商機的規模與持續時間」。
Acree給予Marvell股票「買進」評級。他的新目標價意味著，與周二收盤價相比，仍有31%的上漲空間。
Oppenheimer分析師Rick Schafer周三也表示，「市場氣氛明確的偏樂觀，表現超出預期，因為管理層大幅上調了財務目標。」他並將Marvell目標價從325美元上調至425美元，同時給予Marvell股票「優於大盤」評級。
推動華爾街分析師紛紛上調目標價的主要催化劑，是Marvell亮眼的財測。該公司預估，2031會計年度調整後每股盈餘(EPS)將超過30美元，營收則達到700億至900億美元。作為對照，2026會計年度Marvell每股盈餘為2.84美元，營收為82億美元。
Marvell股價周三下跌1.5%，收在282.73美元，此前周二才大漲5.8%。周二股價在執行長Matt Murphy公布營收目標後立即走高。
今年以來，Marvell股價已上漲238%。隨著AI熱潮推升晶片與網路產品需求，Marvell股價持續受到市場追捧。
paras_en: Baron Weekly reported on Wednesday (the 7th) that Marvell Technology (MRVL-US) has received abundant praise from Wall Street, but for a company that expects revenue to grow 55% to 60% annually over the next five years, such optimism may not be surprising.

According to FactSet data, at least 18 analysts have raised Marvell’s price target as of this week. This reaction came after the chip and networking equipment company announced aggressive growth goals at its investor day in New York.

StoneX analyst Cody Acree is one of the bullish voices; on Tuesday night he lifted Marvell’s price target from $275 to $375. In his research note, Acree wrote that the investor day "redefined the scale and duration of Marvell’s AI opportunity."
Acree gave Marvell a "Buy" rating. His new target implies a 31% upside from Tuesday’s closing price.

Oppenheimer analyst Rick Schafer also said on Wednesday that "the market sentiment is clearly optimistic, outperforming expectations, because management significantly raised its financial targets." He raised Marvell’s target from $325 to $425 and assigned an "Outperform" rating.

The main catalyst driving analysts to raise targets is Marvell’s impressive financial outlook. The company forecasts adjusted FY 2031 earnings per share (EPS) of over $30 and revenue of $70 billion to $90 billion. By comparison, FY 2026 EPS is $2.84 and revenue $8.2 billion.
Marvell’s stock fell 1.5% on Wednesday, closing at $282.73, after having jumped 5.8% on Tuesday. The Tuesday rally came immediately after CEO Matt Murphy announced the revenue targets.
Since the start of the year, Marvell’s share price has risen 238%. Fueled by the AI boom driving demand for chips and networking products, the stock continues to attract strong market interest.

items.title: 市值近25兆美元富可敵國！科技七巨頭包辦三成資本支出  「插頭一拔」全球震盪
items.title_en: Nearly $25 trillion in Market Value, Wealth Rivaling Nations! The Seven Tech Giants Account for About 30% of Capital Spending – Pull One Plug and the World Shakes
paras: 「科技七巨頭」(Magnificent Seven)合計市值接近25兆美元，如果這群科技公司是一個國家，其經濟規模將位居全球第二，超越中國、德國、日本與英國且正逼近美國。當它們成為一股足以撼動經濟的力量，讓人不免擔心經濟力量異常集中所可能產生的問題。
這七家大型科技股包括Alphabet(GOOGL-US)、亞馬遜(AMZN-US)、蘋果(APPL-US)、Meta Platforms(META-US)、微軟(MSFT-US)、輝達(NVDA-US)與特斯拉(TSLA-US)。
Apex Fintech Solutions首席市場分析師暨風險副總裁Mike Treacy說：「這些公司生產的所有產品與提供的服務，就是全世界運轉所依賴的東西，而當你拔掉其中任何一個插頭，一切就會崩潰。」
在這樣的規模下，「科技七巨頭」賺多少錢、花多少錢、借多少錢，以及雇用哪些人，其影響都遠遠超出華爾街。
Treacy指出，這些公司的總體經濟影響「非常巨大」，因為它們往往「成群結隊」行動。例如，2022年利率上升終結廉價資金時代，迫使許多企業、尤其是科技公司，從「不惜一切代價追求成長」的思維，轉向重視獲利能力與削減成本。
近來，人工智慧(AI)熱潮則推動其中許多公司大幅提高資本支出。根據Apex Fintech Solutions與彭博彙整的數據，2026年到目前為止，「科技七巨頭」加上SpaceX(SPCX-US)每年的資本支出約為5800億美元，而標普500指數其餘企業一年的資本支出合計約為1.4兆美元。
換句話說，「科技七巨頭」與SpaceX約占標普500指數總資本支出的30%，凸顯企業投資如今已高度集中在少數大型公司。
令人擔心的是，如果其中一家大型公司開始削減AI建設的支出，其他公司可能跟進，進而導致科技投資全面縮減，並對市場造成重大干擾。
Treacy說：「世界由美國企業運轉，這很好。我們為全世界提供動力，這很好。但如果資本支出的潮流發生轉變，那麼不只美國，全球經濟成長都將面臨一些挑戰。」
paras_en: The “Magnificent Seven” tech giants have a combined market value close to $25 trillion. If these companies were a country, its economy would rank second worldwide, surpassing China, Germany, Japan and the United Kingdom and closing in on the United States. Their sheer economic heft raises concerns about the risks of such concentrated power.
The seven large‑cap tech stocks are Alphabet (GOOGL‑US), Amazon (AMZN‑US), Apple (AAPL‑US), Meta Platforms (META‑US), Microsoft (MSFT‑US), Nvidia (NVDA‑US) and Tesla (TSLA‑US).

Mike Treacy, chief market analyst and vice‑president of risk at Apex Fintech Solutions, said: “All the products these companies make and the services they provide are what the world runs on, and if you pull any one of those plugs, everything collapses.”
At this scale, how much the “Magnificent Seven” earn, spend, borrow and whom they employ has impacts that far exceed Wall Street’s own sphere.

Treacy noted that the overall economic impact of these firms is “enormous” because they tend to act “in packs.” For example, when interest rates rose in 2022 and ended the era of cheap capital, many firms—especially tech companies—shifted from a “grow at all costs” mindset to one that emphasizes profitability and cost cutting.

Recently, the AI boom has driven many of these companies to sharply increase capital expenditures. According to data compiled by Apex Fintech Solutions and Bloomberg, through 2026 the “Magnificent Seven” together with SpaceX (SPCX‑US) have spent roughly $580 billion per year on capex, while the rest of the S&P 500 companies collectively spend about $1.4 trillion annually.

In other words, the “Magnificent Seven” plus SpaceX account for roughly 30 % of total S&P 500 capital spending, highlighting how corporate investment is now heavily concentrated in a handful of mega‑firms.

The worrying scenario is that if one of these large firms begins to cut back AI‑related spending, others may follow, leading to a broad reduction in tech investment and causing significant market disruption.

Treacy said: “The world runs on American companies, and that’s a good thing. We power the globe, and that’s a good thing. But if the tide of capital spending turns, it won’t just be the United States—global economic growth will face challenges.”

items.title: Anthropic僅值1500億美元？遭評「2026年最荒謬IPO」
items.title_en: Anthropic Valued at Only $150 B? Called the "Most Ridiculous IPO of 2026"
paras: 《CNBC》報導，隨著Anthropic朝著在那斯達克掛牌、潛在市值達2兆美元的方向邁進，一家研究機構卻僅給予這家AI公司1,500億美元估值，並警告華爾街即將面臨「投資人輕信程度前所未有的考驗」。
獨立金融研究機構New Constructs周二發布報告，將Anthropic即將進行的首次公開募股稱為「2026年最荒謬IPO」。
New Constructs估計，若要達到Anthropic所期望的估值，該公司必須創造出全球市值最高的科技公司輝達(NVDA-US)過去一年獲利的兩倍。輝達過去四季淨利潤已超過1,900億美元。
而據《路透社》引用Anthropic招股說明書外洩版本的報導，Anthropic 2025年營收為46億美元，但淨損高達420億美元。
Anthropic不斷攀升的營運虧損，加上大量開源模型帶來的競爭，讓New Constructs得出結論：「我們認為Anthropic並沒有一個可行的商業模式。」
該機構寫道，「自從開源模型出現以來，很明顯的，封閉式模型將難以創造獲利。」
New Constructs創辦人兼執行長David Trainer在華爾街以看空IPO聞名，而且過去也曾成功預測部分IPO問題。
New Constructs曾在2019年WeWork計劃上市前，稱其為「2019年最荒謬的IPO」。當時WeWork私人市場估值曾達470億美元，但New Constructs發布報告僅6周後，WeWork便因需求疲弱，以及市場對其財務狀況的強烈批評而撤回IPO計畫。WeWork最終於2023年申請破產。
New Constructs寫道，「雖然Anthropic對社會的貢獻遠高於WeWork，但若估值達到2兆美元，其IPO帶來的風險將放大更多，也可能成為對美國資本市場更大的掠奪。」該機構補充稱，這場IPO的目的並不是為公開市場投資人創造財富，而是為公司的華爾街支持者提供流動性。
New Constructs在2021年Allbirds(BIRD-US)上市時同樣看空。這家鞋類公司當年在那斯達克掛牌，首日交易估值一度達到41億美元。今年稍早，Allbirds將旗下資產出售給American Exchange Group，交易估值約為3,900萬美元，並在此過程中轉向AI領域。
不過，Trainer的公司也曾有看走眼的案例。New Constructs評選的「2020年最荒謬IPO」是DoorDash(DASH-US)，該機構當時也將DoorDash與WeWork相提並論，稱這家外送公司「同樣處於不利地位」。
然而，DoorDash在公開市場的表現相當穩健。該公司2020年12月上市首日股價大漲，市值突破600億美元，此後更進一步攀升至830億美元。
Trainer在2021年受訪時也承認，「瘋狂的事情確實會發生」，而New Constructs並非總能做出正確判斷。「我不能讓這件事困擾我。我必須忠於自己認為正確的判斷。」
Anthropic至今仍未公開招股說明書，因此New Constructs並未看過正式申報文件。不過，該機構引用了多項已經曝光數據，包括《紐約時報》的報導。該報去年9月稱，Anthropic預計到2026年底，年化營收將達到1,000億美元。
Anthropic則在7月底表示，截至當時公司的年化營收已較去年同期成長7倍，達到650億美元。
New Constructs報告還指出，Anthropic曾警告AI可能對人類構成「災難性或存亡級風險」，這也是投資人應該避開這場IPO的另一項理由。
New Constructs寫道，「雖然我們並沒有幸運的成為Anthropic選擇性披露S-1文件的少數對象之一，但外洩財務數據的相關報導，已經揭露了足以讓我們評估這場IPO龐大投資風險的資訊。」
paras_en: CNBC reported that as Anthropic moves toward a Nasdaq listing with a potential market value of $2 trillion, a research firm has assigned the AI company a valuation of just $150 billion and warned that Wall Street is about to face an unprecedented test of investors' gullibility.
Independent financial research firm New Constructs released a report on Tuesday calling Anthropic's upcoming initial public offering the "Most Ridiculous IPO of 2026."

New Constructs estimates that to achieve the valuation Anthropic seeks, the company would have to generate twice the profit that Nvidia (NVDA-US), the world’s most valuable tech firm, earned over the past year. Nvidia’s net profit over the last four quarters has already exceeded $190 billion.
According to a Reuters story citing a leaked version of Anthropic’s prospectus, the company’s 2025 revenue is projected at $4.6 billion, but its net loss would be a staggering $42 billion.
Anthropic’s ever‑growing operating losses, combined with intense competition from open‑source models, lead New Constructs to conclude: "We believe Anthropic does not have a viable business model."
The firm wrote, "Since the advent of open‑source models, it has become clear that closed‑source models will struggle to generate profit."
New Constructs founder and CEO David Trainer is known on Wall Street for his bearish stance on IPOs and has previously correctly predicted problems with several offerings.

In 2019, New Constructs labeled WeWork’s planned listing as "the most ridiculous IPO of 2019." At the time, WeWork’s private‑market valuation had reached $47 billion, but just six weeks after the firm’s report, WeWork withdrew its IPO amid weak demand and harsh criticism of its finances, eventually filing for bankruptcy in 2023.

New Constructs wrote, "Although Anthropic’s contribution to society far exceeds that of WeWork, a $2 trillion valuation would magnify the risks of its IPO and could become a greater predatory force on U.S. capital markets." The firm added that the purpose of the offering is not to create wealth for public investors but to provide liquidity for Anthropic’s Wall Street backers.

New Constructs also took a bearish view when Allbirds (BIRD-US) went public in 2021. The footwear company debuted on Nasdaq with a peak first‑day valuation of $4.1 billion. Earlier this year, Allbirds sold its assets to the American Exchange Group for roughly $39 million and pivoted toward AI.
However, Trainer’s firm has had missteps. Its "most ridiculous IPO of 2020" pick was DoorDash (DASH-US), which it then compared to WeWork, calling the delivery firm "similarly disadvantaged."
DoorDash’s market performance has been solid. The company’s shares surged on its December 2020 debut, pushing its market cap past $60 billion, and later climbing to about $83 billion.

In a 2021 interview, Trainer admitted, "Crazy things do happen," and that New Constructs does not always get it right. "I can’t let this bother me. I have to stay true to the judgments I believe are correct."

Anthropic has not yet released a formal prospectus, so New Constructs has not seen an official filing. The firm does cite several publicly disclosed data points, including a New York Times report that last September projected Anthropic’s annual revenue would reach $100 billion by the end of 2026.
Anthropic said at the end of July that its annualized revenue had grown seven‑fold year‑over‑year to $65 billion.

The New Constructs report also notes that Anthropic warned AI could pose "catastrophic or existential risks" to humanity, which the firm cites as another reason investors should steer clear of the IPO.

New Constructs wrote, "While we were not among the lucky few selected by Anthropic for a selective S‑1 disclosure, the leaked financial data reports have revealed enough information for us to assess the massive investment risk of this IPO."

items.title: 黃仁勳焦慮AI需求降溫！傳輝達再砸10億美元加碼人形機器人企業Figure
items.title_en: Jensen Huang Worried About Cooling AI Demand! Nvidia Adds Another $1 Billion to Humanoid Robot Company Figure
paras: 外媒最新報導指出，AI晶片巨擘輝達近期正討論向人形機器人製造商Figure追加投資10億美元，該融資計畫此前從未對外披露。輝達已是Figure的投資方，一年前曾以相同估值參與其超過10億美元的融資。Figure此輪融資的投前估值約為380億美元
《The Information》引述知情人士報導，除加碼機器人賽道外，輝達的投資版圖正持續擴大。知情人士透露，輝達也可能向兩類新創公司注資：一類是協助開發其Nemotron開源模型的公司，另一類是開發其他AI應用的團隊，例如輝達已同意斥資60億美元獲取Poolside的軟體授權並聘用其員工，以推動Nemotron模型的研發，Poolside團隊今年剛推出開放權重的Laguna AI模型。
輝達執行長黃仁勳正主導此投資佈局。儘管手握990億美元現金及證券，且現金流充沛，黃仁勳仍對公司的全球市場地位保持警惕。
他坦言，擔憂AI需求降溫或出現替代性晶片產品，因此希望透過財力推動數千個AI模型發展，降低對OpenAI等少數大客戶的依賴。在今年7月為止的半年裡，三大客戶貢獻了輝達總銷售額的44%。
一名投資AI基礎設施和應用的投資人表示，如果參與黃仁勳的戰略決策，他會盡一切努力推動數千個模型服務數千種不同場景。
paras_en: Foreign media reports that Nvidia, the AI chip giant, is currently discussing a $1 billion additional investment in humanoid robot maker Figure, a financing plan that has not been disclosed before. Nvidia is already an investor in Figure, having participated in a financing round of over $1 billion a year ago at the same valuation. Figure’s pre‑money valuation for this round is about $38 billion.

The Information, citing sources, reported that beyond expanding its robot bets, Nvidia’s investment scope is continuing to broaden. Insiders say Nvidia may also fund two types of startups: one that helps develop its open‑source Nemotron model, and another that builds other AI applications. For example, Nvidia has agreed to spend $6 billion to acquire software licenses from Poolside and hire its staff to advance Nemotron development; Poolside’s team just released the open‑weight Laguna AI model this year.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is steering this investment strategy. Even though the company holds $99 billion in cash and securities and enjoys strong cash flow, Huang remains vigilant about Nvidia’s global market position.

He admitted he worries about a slowdown in AI demand or the emergence of alternative chip products, so he wants to use Nvidia’s financial muscle to push the development of thousands of AI models and reduce reliance on a few large customers such as OpenAI. In the first half of the year through July, the three biggest customers accounted for 44 % of Nvidia’s total sales.

An investor focused on AI infrastructure and applications said that if he were part of Jensen Huang’s strategic decision‑making, he would do everything possible to drive thousands of models serving thousands of different scenarios.

items.title: 三星秀150毫米超大玻璃基板、最高30層堆疊 已送AI客戶測試
items.title_en: Samsung Showcases 150mm Ultra‑Large Glass Substrate, Up to 30‑Layer Stacking, Sent to AI Customers for Testing
paras: 三星電機在KPCA韓國封裝展展示新一代玻璃核心基板，推出150毫米超大尺寸、最高支援30層增層堆疊的樣品，瞄準下一代AI與高效能運算（HPC）晶片封裝需求。三星已向主要AI客戶送樣測試，並布局上游玻璃芯材料供應，推進玻璃基板商用化。
此舉標誌著三星在下一代高效能運算（HPC）與AI晶片封裝基板領域，成功完成從傳統有機FCBGA向玻璃基異構集成的關鍵技術跨越，直接迎戰英特爾、台積電、京東方等全球對手的技術競賽。
隨著GPU、HBM記憶體及小晶片（Chiplet）整合程度提高，AI伺服器晶片功耗持續攀升，傳統ABF有機載板面臨翹曲、高溫穩定性不足與高速訊號損耗等挑戰。
玻璃基板具備熱膨脹係數與矽接近、低介電損耗及高尺寸穩定性等優勢，成為下一代封裝的重要發展方向，大尺寸與高層數堆疊則是量產的關鍵門檻。
尺寸放大 可搭載更多晶片
三星此次展示的150毫米玻璃基板，相較先前業界主流110毫米級產品，可用面積增加，單塊基板能承載更多小晶片與HBM記憶體組合，以滿足超大尺寸AI晶片封裝需求。
最高30層堆疊也是展品亮點。多層增層製程中，每一層都須完成精細線路製作、層間精準對位及玻璃通孔（TGV）互連；隨著層數增加，對位偏差、翹曲與分層失效風險也隨之升高。
三星電機結合多年FCBGA高層基板製程經驗，以及與住友化學合資成立的Glass EM所開發的專用玻璃芯材料，整合多層增層與TGV垂直互連技術，實現30層結構穩定成型，透過高密度垂直通孔，提供多晶片間的高速訊號通道。
上游材料布局同步推進
在材料供應方面，三星電機與日本住友化學合資成立Glass EM，於韓國平澤建設玻璃芯產線，計畫2027年下半年啟動量產，為玻璃基板提供上游材料保障。
三星也已向主要AI客戶送樣，進行可靠性、高低溫循環與高速訊號完整性驗證，目標用於下一代伺服器AI晶片封裝。
三星的技術路線採用超快雷射在玻璃上製作TGV，再透過填銅與多層增層布線，實現高密度垂直互連，主要用途是算力晶片封裝的電訊號互連。
走向量產仍有挑戰
全球玻璃基板競爭已進入技術驗證與送樣階段。三星這套150毫米、30層方案，將在基板尺寸、堆疊層數、TGV良率及成本等方面，與英特爾、台積電及京東方等業者競爭。
不過，大尺寸、高層數玻璃基板仍須解決TGV填銅均勻性、多層增層熱應力控制、晶片組裝後的長期可靠性，以及面板級量產良率等問題。
三星電機表示，將持續縮小線寬與線距、開發更高規格產品，布局AI伺服器、自動駕駛及高效能網路晶片封裝市場。
paras_en: Samsung Electronics displayed its next‑generation glass core substrate at the KPCA Korea Packaging Expo, unveiling a 150 mm ultra‑large sample that supports up to 30 stacked layers, targeting the packaging needs of next‑generation AI and high‑performance computing (HPC) chips. Samsung has already shipped samples to major AI customers for testing and is securing upstream glass core material supply to advance commercialisation of glass substrates.

This move marks Samsung’s successful leap from traditional organic FCBGA to glass‑based heterogeneous integration in the next‑generation HPC and AI chip packaging substrate arena, directly challenging global rivals such as Intel, TSMC and BOE in the technology race.

As GPU, HBM memory and chiplet integration intensify, AI server chip power consumption keeps rising, and conventional organic ABF substrates face warpage, insufficient high‑temperature stability and high‑speed signal loss issues.

Glass substrates offer advantages such as a coefficient of thermal expansion close to silicon, low dielectric loss and high dimensional stability, making them a key development direction for next‑generation packaging; large size and high‑layer stacking are the critical thresholds for volume production.
Larger size enables more chips to be mounted

The 150 mm glass substrate Samsung showcased, compared with the industry‑standard 110 mm products, provides a larger usable area, allowing a single panel to accommodate more chiplets and HBM memory stacks to meet the demands of ultra‑large AI chip packages.

The up‑to‑30‑layer stack is another highlight. In the multi‑layer build‑up process, each layer requires fine line patterning, precise inter‑layer alignment and glass through‑via (TGV) interconnects; as the layer count rises, alignment errors, warpage and delamination risks also increase.

Samsung Electronics leverages years of experience in high‑layer FCBGA processing and the specialised glass core material developed by Glass EM, a joint venture with Sumitomo Chemical, integrating multi‑layer build‑up and TGV vertical interconnect technology to achieve a stable 30‑layer structure, using high‑density vertical vias to provide high‑speed signal paths between multiple chips.
Upstream material positioning proceeds in parallel

For material supply, Samsung Electronics and Japan’s Sumitomo Chemical have formed the Glass EM joint venture, building a glass‑core production line in Pyeongtaek, Korea, with mass production slated to start in the second half of 2027, securing upstream material assurance for glass substrates.

Samsung has also sent samples to key AI customers for reliability, high‑ and low‑temperature cycling and high‑speed signal integrity verification, aiming for use in next‑generation server AI chip packaging.

Samsung’s technical approach uses ultra‑fast lasers to create TGVs in glass, followed by copper filling and multi‑layer routing to achieve high‑density vertical interconnects, primarily for electrical signal interconnection in compute‑chip packages.
Path to volume production still faces challenges

Global competition in glass substrates has entered the technology validation and sampling stage. Samsung’s 150 mm, 30‑layer solution will compete with Intel, TSMC and BOE on substrate size, stack count, TGV yield and cost.

However, large‑size, high‑layer glass substrates must still overcome issues such as uniform copper filling of TGVs, thermal stress control in multi‑layer build‑up, long‑term reliability after chip assembly, and panel‑level production yields.

Samsung Electronics said it will continue to shrink line widths and spacings, develop higher‑spec products and position itself in the AI server, autonomous‑driving and high‑performance networking chip packaging markets.

items.title: 花旗調升台積電目標價至4000元 看好2027年營收成長逾四成
items.title_en: Citi Raises TSMC Target Price to NT$4,000, Bullish on Over 40% Revenue Growth by 2027
paras: 花旗看好台積電(2330-TW) 營收成長前景，預估到2027年的營收成長率可能超過40%，維持「買進」評等，並將目標價由新台幣3,800元上調至4,000元。
花旗在最新研究報告中指出，受惠於AI運算需求強勁、AI代理可能帶來額外成長空間，以及共同封裝光學（CPO）網路週期興起，台積電到2027年的營收成長率可能超過40%。
花旗分析師表示，台積電多數AI晶片客戶，包括輝達(NVDA-US) 、AMD(AMD-US)及博通(AVGO-US) ，預計成長將加速，帶動台積電明年AI相關營收可能接近倍增。
除了既有AI運算需求，AI代理帶來的潛在成長空間，以及CPO網路週期的興起，也是花旗看好台積電營收展望的因素。
隨著AI晶片客戶成長加快，花旗預期，市場對台積電獲利的平均預估將持續上修。此次調高目標價，也反映花旗對其強勁營收前景的看法。
資本支出方面，花旗預估，在營收前景支撐下，台積電2027年與2028年的資本支出可能進一步提高，分別達810億美元及900億美元。
花旗在看好AI相關營收成長的同時，也預期台積電未來兩年的資本支出規模將持續擴大。
高盛日前也將台積電目標價由3,100元上調至3,300元，維持「買進」評級，並調高資本支出預估，主因是看好AI需求持續擴張。
高盛分析師Evelyn Yu指出，AI需求持續擴及GPU、網路晶片與伺服器CPU，其中代理型AI帶動CPU需求增強，是過去一年來的關鍵變化。
該行預估，以美元計算，台積電2026年及2027年營收將分別年增42%與36.9%，毛利率則達67.2%與67.5%。
隨著AI需求擴張，高盛也將台積電2027年及2028年資本支出預估，由780億及820億美元，均上調至850億美元。
paras_en: Citi is optimistic about TSMC (2330-TW) revenue growth prospects, estimating that revenue growth could exceed 40% by 2027, maintaining a "Buy" rating and raising the target price from NT$3,800 to NT$4,000.

In its latest research report, Citi notes that strong AI computing demand, additional growth potential from AI agents, and the emergence of the Co‑Packaged Optics (CPO) network cycle could push TSMC's revenue growth rate past 40% by 2027.

Citi analysts say that most of TSMC's AI chip customers, including Nvidia (NVDA-US), AMD (AMD-US) and Broadcom (AVGO-US), are expected to accelerate growth, potentially nearly doubling TSMC's AI‑related revenue next year.
Beyond existing AI computing demand, the potential growth from AI agents and the rise of the CPO network cycle are also factors behind Citi's positive revenue outlook for TSMC.
As AI chip customers grow faster, Citi expects market estimates of TSMC's earnings to be continually revised upward. The target‑price increase reflects Citi's view of a strong revenue outlook.
On the capital‑expenditure side, Citi projects that, supported by the revenue outlook, TSMC's capex could rise further in 2027 and 2028 to $81 billion and $90 billion respectively.
While bullish on AI‑related revenue growth, Citi also expects TSMC's capital‑expenditure scale to keep expanding over the next two years.
Goldman Sachs recently raised its TSMC target price from $3,100 to $3,300, kept a "Buy" rating, and increased its capex estimate, citing confidence in sustained AI demand expansion.
Goldman analyst Evelyn Yu highlighted that AI demand continues to spread across GPUs, networking chips and server CPUs, with agent‑type AI boosting CPU demand—a key shift over the past year.
The firm estimates that, in USD terms, TSMC's revenue will grow 42% in 2026 and 36.9% in 2027, with gross margins reaching 67.2% and 67.5% respectively.
With AI demand expanding, Goldman also raised its capex forecasts for TSMC in 2027 and 2028 from $78 billion and $82 billion to $85 billion each.

◆EUR/USD
全球債券市場拋售暫歇，提振風險偏好，但昨日中國數據顯示9月外匯儲備較前月減少380.7億美元，規模創六個月新低，而且FED會議紀錄公布前賣盤湧現，導致澳幣及紐元承壓，並隨著西班牙宣布提前舉行大選，拖累歐元兌美元受限於1.1264高點。

隨著德國上半年出口意外強勁，德國外貿協會(BGA)將今年出口增長預期上調至1%，並據德國聯邦統計局表示，受建築業產出增長推動，8月德國工業生產較前月升2.0%超出預期，而且法國央行(BOF)總裁穆蘭稱，法國的經濟形勢嚴峻，但現階段無需尋求歐洲央行(ECB)介入，惟市場擔憂法國財政狀況不斷惡化及明年可能導致嚴重分岐的總統選舉，而且油價上漲和歐洲公債收益率攀升，削弱對歐元的信心，推動歐元兌美元跌至1.1164低點價位。預估今日歐元兌美元阻力於1.1200-20，支撐於1.1110-30。

週三萊斯銀行集團公布英國9月房屋價格較前月與上年同期均持平，但皆不及預期，並按季度計算，房屋價格下跌0.2%，而且8月錄得2023年以來首次較去年同期下跌，打擊英鎊兌美元自1.3275高點下跌。隨著美國公債收益率在FED會議紀錄公布前重拾升勢及美圓普遍走強，而且市場聚焦英國10月28日的首份預算案，擴大英鎊兌美元跌幅至1.3190低點價位。預估今日英鎊兌美元阻力於1.3210-30，支撐於1.3110-30。

外匯市場參與者周三關注聯準會9月貨幣政策會議紀要。紀要顯示，多數聯邦公開市場委員會(FOMC)官員認為，今年年底前還可能再升息一次。
FOMC上個月一致投票決定將聯邦資金利率上調25個基點，為3年多來首次升息。同時，FOMC更新後的點陣圖也暗示今年還可能進一步升息。聯準會主席華許(Kevin Warsh)則在會後記者會上表示，讓通膨回落至央行2%的目標，仍是一項重大挑戰。
會議紀要指出，「關於本次會議之後的貨幣政策前景，多數與會者認為，在今年年底前進一步上調聯邦資金利率目標區間可能是適當的。」
紀要也顯示，所有FOMC官員都支持9月升息。
不過，這份紀要公布之際，市場對FOMC本月底再次升息的預期已較9月升息後大幅下降，主要受到近期部分官員偏鴿派的談話，以及美國經濟成長、通膨與勞動市場數據的影響。

歐元受法國財政危機拖累
美元走強另一助力是歐元周三走跌。歐元兌美元下跌0.6%，至1歐元兌1.1195美元。

法國今年財政赤字預計將達國內生產毛額(GDP)的5.4%，公共債務則接近GDP的120%。
法國政府上周公布2027年預算案，目標透過削減540億歐元的支出，將財政赤字目標控制在GDP的5%。
同時，法國在明年4月與5月舉行兩輪選舉前，也面臨政治不確定性。總統大選領先者、極右派政黨國民聯盟(National Rally)候選人勒龐，以及該黨黨魁Jordan Bardella周二公布主要預算方案，目標在2032年前節省1,400億歐元。

paras_en: The dollar strengthened on Wednesday (the 7th), rising to a near 18‑month high, buoyed by Fed meeting minutes that indicated a possible further rate hike and by the weakness of the euro and pound. The euro and pound were pressured by a renewed wave of global bond sell‑offs, bearing downward pressure.
In the New York close, the dollar index (DXY), which tracks the dollar against six major currencies, rose 0.4% to 102.24, briefly touching its highest level since April 9, 2025.

Forex market participants on Wednesday focused on the Fed’s September monetary policy meeting minutes. The minutes showed that most Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) members think another rate hike could still be possible before the end of the year.

Last month the FOMC voted unanimously to raise the federal funds rate by 25 basis points, the first hike in more than three years. At the same time, the updated FOMC dot‑plot also hinted at the possibility of further hikes this year. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said in the post‑meeting press conference that bringing inflation down to the central bank’s 2% target remains a major challenge.

The minutes noted, “Regarding the monetary policy outlook after this meeting, most participants believe that a further increase in the target range for the federal funds rate may be appropriate before the end of this year.”
The minutes also showed that all FOMC members supported a September rate hike.

However, as the minutes were released, market expectations for another FOMC hike at the end of the month had fallen sharply from after the September hike, mainly due to recent dovish remarks by some officials and the impact of U.S. economic growth, inflation and labor market data.
According to the CME FedWatch tool, the market now sees an almost 83% probability that rates will remain unchanged at the end of the month, up from about 54% a month ago.
Euro weighed down by France’s fiscal crisis
Another boost to the dollar’s strength was the euro’s decline on Wednesday. The euro fell 0.6% against the dollar to $1.1195 per euro.

As France’s fiscal crisis deepens and Spain’s politics stall, market risk sentiment across the continent is under pressure. France’s 10‑year government bond yield has risen to its highest level since early 2000.
France’s fiscal deficit this year is projected to reach 5.4% of GDP, with public debt close to 120% of GDP.
The French government unveiled its 2027 budget last week, aiming to cut €54 billion in spending and keep the fiscal deficit target at 5% of GDP.

At the same time, France faces political uncertainty ahead of two rounds of elections in April and May next year. National Rally leader Jordan Bardella, the party’s frontrunner in the presidential race, announced on Tuesday a major budget plan targeting €140 billion in savings by 2032.
Pound weakens as UK 30‑year gilt yield hits a 1998 high
A global bond sell‑off on Wednesday spread to the UK, pushing the 30‑year gilt yield to its highest level since January 1998.
Just a day earlier, UK Treasury Secretary John Healey met with the main dealers in the gilt market, the so‑called Gilt‑edged Market Makers (GEMMs).
The Treasury said the meeting discussed the severe external environment facing the UK and global economies, including geopolitical developments and financial market conditions.
The pound fell 0.5% against the dollar to $1.3213 per pound.

paras: 美國8月貿易逆差擴大至1,056億美元，創2025年初以來最大，且超出市場預期。AI建設帶動半導體與設備進口，加上能源成本上升及關稅政策干擾，推升進口額至歷史新高，貿易恐再度拖累第三季經濟成長。不過，強勁內需也顯示消費與企業投資仍具支撐力。
美國商務部周二(6日)公布，8月商品與服務貿易逆差較前月擴大13.7%，高於市場預估的約1,020億美元，7月逆差則修正為928億美元。8月進口月增4.3%至4,208億美元，出口僅增1.4%至3,152億美元，成長速度明顯落後。

AI建設拉動進口 半導體增額創紀錄

美國第二季內需增速創逾三年半最快，消費與AI相關設備投資強勁。8月消費支出及核心資本財訂單、出貨數據顯示，這股動能延續至第三季，企業則持續依靠進口滿足需求。

貿易已連續三季拖累美國國內生產毛額(GDP)，經濟學家估計，第三季拖累幅度可能達2.5個百分點。最新數據公布前，亞特蘭大聯準銀行GDPNow模型估計，淨出口將拉低第三季GDP成長率2.59個百分點，將是2025年初以來最大拖累。

paras_en: U.S. August trade deficit widened to $105.6 billion, the biggest since early 2025 and above market expectations. AI build‑out drove semiconductor and equipment imports, while higher energy costs and tariff policy disruptions pushed total imports to a historic high, threatening to again drag down third‑quarter economic growth. Nevertheless, strong domestic demand shows consumption and corporate investment remain supportive.

The U.S. Department of Commerce reported on Tuesday (the 6th) that the goods‑and‑services trade deficit for August expanded 13.7% from the prior month, exceeding the market forecast of roughly $102 billion; the July deficit was revised to $92.8 billion. August imports rose 4.3% month‑over‑month to $420.8 billion, while exports increased only 1.4% to $315.2 billion, a clearly slower growth rate.

AI construction pulled imports higher, with semiconductor imports hitting a record increase. August goods imports rose 5.3% month‑over‑month to $342.2 billion, while goods exports grew 2.2% to $205.7 billion. After inflation adjustment, the goods trade deficit expanded to $114.7 billion, the largest since March 2025.

Imports of capital goods—including computers and peripherals, semiconductors and telecom equipment—rose by $6.2 billion from the prior month. Semiconductor imports alone jumped $2.4 billion, setting a new single‑month increase record, while civil aircraft and telecom equipment imports also rose, reflecting the continued reliance on overseas supply for the AI investment boom.

Imports of industrial raw materials, including oil and petroleum products, increased by $9.1 billion, while exports rose $6.3 billion, with crude oil exports up $2.0 billion. Non‑monetary gold imports and exports also grew. By contrast, services exports were roughly flat, weighed down by U.S. visitor spending falling to its lowest level since August 2023.

U.S. domestic demand in the second quarter grew at the fastest pace in more than three and a half years, with strong consumer spending and AI‑related equipment investment. August consumer outlays and core capital‑goods orders and shipments indicate this momentum will carry into the third quarter, as firms continue to rely on imports to meet demand.

Trade has been a drag on U.S. gross domestic product (GDP) for three consecutive quarters, and economists estimate the third‑quarter drag could reach 2.5 percentage points. Ahead of the latest data release, the Atlanta Fed’s GDPNow model projected that net exports would shave 2.59 percentage points off third‑quarter GDP growth, the biggest drag since early 2025.

However, market forecasts for third‑quarter GDP growth are generally above an annualized 3%, with expectations that consumer spending will offset the import‑related drag, improving on the second quarter’s 2.2% rate.

Former President Trump argues that higher tariffs help narrow the deficit, yet imports keep climbing. Tariff changes, war‑driven oil‑price volatility and supply‑chain challenges also cause unadjusted monthly trade figures to swing sharply.

By country, the U.S. deficit with Canada rose to its highest level since early 2025. After trade talks broke down in August, firms in both nations rushed to ship goods before tariffs took effect; the U.S. imposed a 50% tariff on billions of dollars of Canadian goods starting August 22, prompting a Canadian retaliation. Deficits with Mexico and Vietnam also edged higher to new highs, and the deficit with Taiwan, a key semiconductor supplier, increased as well.
